description: A C# game engine in which a program opens a window, draws each frame with plain static calls named as raylib's functions are, and draws Dear ImGui in the same frame, over SDL3, Vulkan and Slang, with an ECS and source-generated behaviors underneath.
releaseNotes:
The readback pool's test draws a frame of its own work in every slot before its count and names each buffer the device holds past it, so it holds on any machine and a leak still fails it.
F2 writes a screenshot of the frame into a folder beside the program and F3 shows the performance window, each key set by a call that moves it or turns it off.
The client records a running app through ./e3d record and waits for the file, ./e3d animate and build/animate.py make captures on disk into one animation with Pillow or the engine's writers, and the README shows Ore turning from day to night as their first use.
A run is recorded as an animated GIF or PNG by StartRecording and the record command, a picture at each step of the app's clock taken by the frame's capture and written on a worker once the last is back, in BevyCSharp's words and with its writers.
The readback pool keeps as many staging buffers of a size as frames can be in flight and one, and its test counts after the dispatches' own buffers are let go and holds both counts to that, so a slower device's timing no longer fails it while a leak still does.
Global illumination reads a mesh a compute shader wrote, its count read back without a wait once a dispatch binds its buffers and its triangles written into the scene field's pool on the GPU from its positions, so a compute-written wall tints the block beside it.
A mesh is drawn from shader buffers a compute shader wrote through LoadMeshFromShaderBuffers, its vertex count turned into an indirect draw's arguments by one dispatch over the frame's draws ahead of the frame, culled by the box SetMeshBoundingBox gives it, with the shaders_compute_mesh example meshing a hill on the GPU each frame.
A shader buffer is read back without holding the program through ReadShaderBufferAsync, whose copy goes to the GPU with the next submission after the dispatches before it, IsShaderReadbackReady saying when it is made, GetShaderReadback reading it and UnloadShaderReadback giving its staging buffer back to a pool.
With the screen's probes left out and a glow light lit, probes stand for the glow lights alone, marching to them once a tile and tracing nothing else, so a pixel reads their light at a cost the lights do not change, Ore at night with sixty-four lit drawing in 2.50 ms where 9.67.
title: 3DEngine
